paragraphs: In [Sotah 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.30a.3) he speaks in the name of Rav. Perhaps he is [Rabbah bar Itai, who lived in Rav’s time, as explained in the entry Rava bar Itai. In [Sotah 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.30a.3), too, the reading should be “Rabbah bar Itai said in the name of Rabbah.” This requires further investigation.]

notes.text: On [Hyman’s printed page](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=238), the Isi notice stops after “perhaps he is.” The bracketed text in the supplied transcription follows under the next heading, Rabbah bar Itai.
The linked vocalized Bavli has Rav Asi or Rabbah ben Isi transmitting in Rav’s name. [Heilprin’s short notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3153&lang=en) gives both names.
Bomberg has Rav Ashi first and Rabbah ben Isi second. Munich 95 names Rabbah bar Isi twice, first citing Rav and then Rav Yosef. Hyman’s proposed reading, Itai citing Rabbah, remains conjectural.
